name: WEINMANN FEEDBOT F-500 stud-feeding robot
summary: Six-axis industrial robot with servo grippers that takes standard studs, special studs and top and bottom plates from storage and sets them into a WEINMANN FRAMETEQ frame work station, so timber-frame walls, gables and window and door frames are framed automatically. Part of HOMAG's smartPrefab robot line.

germany.statusNote: Sold on request by WEINMANN, HOMAG's timber-construction brand. The first robot framing line went to a German prefab maker in early 2017, and WeberHaus runs the robot-based smartPrefab framing station at Rheinau-Linx. HOMAG's own pages could not be read by the polite reader, so no German contact details or price are given here; the US dealer Stiles Machinery also sells it.

specs.label: Parts handled
specs.value: top and bottom plates, standard and special studs
specs.quote: The FEEDBOT F-500 streamlines the automated insertion of top and bottom plates, along with both standard and specialized studs, for efficient assembly.

specs.label: Gripper
specs.quote: The FEEDBOT F-500 delivers top-tier precision in stud placement with servo motor-driven robot grippers

specs.label: Works with
specs.quote: The FEEDBOT F-500, seamlessly incorporated into the FRAMETEQ series

specs.label: Stud placing cycle
specs.conditions: planned for a Swedish line in 2017 (one wall element in 7 minutes)
specs.quote: the robot places a stud into the framework every 7 seconds

specs.label: Element types
specs.value: inner and outer walls, gable and mitre walls, window and door structures
specs.quote: not only inner and outer walls but also gable walls and miter walls, as well as window and door structures, are manufactured fully automatically

notes: Stationary 6-axis robot (KUKA arm in HOMAG livery in the maker photos) beside the frame work station.
Studs come from a random 'stud tower' fed by a WBZ 160 carpentry machine and from a standard-stud store; plates are fed on driven rollers.
The 6-axis motion lets it change the insertion method per stud, which helps with crooked timber (HOMAG via Wood & Panel).
Maximum stud weight and workpiece size range are on HOMAG pages that the polite reader could not open, so they are not given here.
